reviews.text: A leading veterinary hospital in Madrid. I took my dog ​​to the ophthalmology clinic. The examination was very thorough, just like the ones they do at my regular checkups. The service was excellent. The consultation fee was high.
Excellent service and professionalism.

Cotton has a chronic heart condition. He arrived with a blue tongue, was seen immediately, and was diagnosed with pneumonia. He was hospitalized for two days. The staff was wonderful! They explained everything perfectly. The cardiologist was lovely. Regarding the hospital itself, the staff was very attentive, the facilities were excellent, and I have absolutely no negative comments. It was my first time there, and I will continue to take Cotton there.

I couldn't be more grateful to the ophthalmology team at Puchol Veterinary Hospital, led by Fernando Laguna and including Marcela and Diana.

My podenco had been suffering from a foxtail lodged in her tear duct for five months, causing inflammation and eye discharge due to an infection that we hadn't been able to resolve despite visiting other clinics. During the first visit, Marcela identified the cause of the problem, which was a crucial step towards finally finding a solution. Since then, I've been in constant communication with the team, who have supported me throughout the entire process with excellent care.

Finally, Fernando Laguna successfully removed the foxtail through microsurgery, and my podenco has been discharged. After so many months of worry and uncertainty, I feel a great sense of relief.

My little one isn't particularly mischievous, and we always try to prevent foxtails from getting in her eyes, but it only takes a moment of carelessness for one to get stuck where it shouldn't.

Thank you, Fernando, Marcela, and Diana, for your professionalism, dedication, and kindness, and for never giving up on finding a solution. You have restored my peace of mind and, above all, my dog's well-being.

This hospital's policy is MRI first, then treatment or surgery. They don't do examinations, X-rays, or less expensive tests. A visit costs 300 euros.

If the family can't afford the MRI, you weigh the animal and offer your condolences. I've experienced this firsthand, and I couldn't believe it. And if the family asks for a second chance, you give them medication without knowing what the problem might be... because you don't want to do other, less expensive tests... offering condolences when the dog is HEALTHY... it's outrageous.
A very comprehensive veterinary hospital with all kinds of medical specialties.
We went with a suspicion of a heart murmur and within half an hour we had the first consultation and an echocardiogram done with the diagnosis, the treatment was very kind and professional.

I took my dog ​​🐕 because he'd had a lot of ear problems for years, and this hospital was recommended to me, and I'm truly delighted. He's been treated by Dr. Lucía in Dermatology, and after many tests and treatments, she recommended ear surgery. The surgical team, especially Enrique, who attended to me from the very beginning, and the rest of the team, is excellent. I want to thank them for everything they're doing to improve my dog's quality of life by reducing the amount of medication he needs, and seeing how well he's doing, is wonderful. Thank you all so much for the kind treatment from reception until we leave the hospital. Thank you for taking such good care of us and our little companions.

We've been waiting four hours for some cat blood compatibility tests that were supposed to take an hour, all because the poor girl in charge of the lab is the same receptionist. For a bill of several thousand euros, they're unnecessarily cutting corners on staff.
Thank you so much
The way they treat our furry friends is wonderful and the facilities are fantastic.
Thank you so much

I don't know the emergency hospital; I took my blind dog to see the specialist Manuel Villagrasa, and everything I'd heard about him falls short. I even know some of his students who value him above all others. He's the best veterinary ophthalmologist in Spain and probably in Europe. He's also a wonderful person, genuinely concerned about his patients. I would ask everyone who works with him to learn from him every day and to strive to be like him, so that when he takes his well-deserved vacation, we'll know that there are people who have followed in his footsteps, and we can all continue to be in good hands.
Thank you so much
Everyone was very professional and tactful despite the difficult situation with my dog. Paula from neurology was outstanding. Thank you so much for everything.

Incredibly grateful to Paula, the neurologist who treated my Boo. She gave us all the empathy, understanding, and love in the world during difficult times. We had to put her to sleep, and she stayed much later than her scheduled appointment time, among other things that restored our faith in humanity. Thank you, Paula, you made this pain a little less intense.
Thank you so much
Thank you so much

My little dog Mati was hospitalized for four days, and I must commend the excellent care we both received.

I would like to highlight the impeccable service from Geyleen in Admissions; she was incredibly professional and empathetic. Celia, the veterinary assistant, was lovely when Mati was admitted, Laura, the veterinarian who received us upon admission, was very kind, and finally, Ane Saiz, the veterinarian, called me every day to keep me updated, providing exquisite care, thorough information, and showing empathy and understanding.

I hope this sincere praise reaches the hospital's management and that they recognize the work of these professionals. We need to celebrate each other more often; in difficult situations, receiving good treatment is invaluable. Sincerely, Concha Vázquez.

We couldn't be happier with the treatment and consideration the entire team has shown us and our furry daughter. I'm so grateful that, despite the misfortune of the illness we've had to endure, we've been fortunate enough to find such a wonderful team.

My dog ​​was in the ICU for a week with acute kidney failure, and I have to say I have absolutely no complaints. They have incredible resources and staff. The care she received, both for her and for us, was excellent during her stay, and I especially want to thank Paula for her professionalism. The problem arose when she was discharged. My dog ​​had improved significantly with fluid therapy alone, but her kidneys hadn't fully recovered. The cause of the kidney failure was unknown, though they suspected, by process of elimination, that it might have been poisoning from ingesting something. She tested negative for all infectious diseases, but they told us that the results of a urine test were still pending and that they would call us with them. The day after her discharge, I called because my dog ​​didn't seem well; she was barely eating and remained lethargic. We repeated the test at our regular vet, and her kidneys had worsened slightly. I called to inform them, and they said it could be normal and that we needed to give her more time to monitor her progress. Ten days after her discharge, I had to call myself to ask about the missing test results because it seemed strange that so much time had passed. They told me to email the hospital ward requesting them. I did, and to my surprise, when they sent me the results, my dog ​​had tested positive for leptospirosis, a very serious zoonotic disease. No one had called me or sent me the results. And when I requested them, they sent them to me as if I were sending an invoice. I had to call numerous times to ask them to please put me through to a veterinarian who had treated my dog, and after several hours, they finally called me to tell me how to proceed with my dog ​​and what treatment to give her. I don't know if they misplaced the test results, if they forgot to call me, or where the problem arose. But it's a very serious infection that can kill a dog if not treated promptly. It required sufficient attention and urgency to call me the moment the results came back and give me a clear and quick protocol.

If this hadn't happened, I would have honestly given them 5 stars, but the mistake was serious and could have ended very badly.
For a long time they came with my pets and treated me well; they weren't always right, but that's human.

I went to Puchol Hospital with my dog, desperate after three months of X-rays, ultrasounds, endoscopy, antibiotics, and anti-inflammatories, with her respiratory problems steadily worsening. I was immediately given an appointment with internal medicine. That same day, she had a CT scan, and the next day she was in the operating room for a tracheotomy. I must say that the surgical team's care couldn't have been better; before the operation, I received a call from the surgeon to inform me about the procedure, they also called me afterward, and every day while she was hospitalized. After being discharged, she has had several complications, and I have always received a prompt and reassuring response. I have felt at all times that she was in the best hands. The process isn't over; although she is better, she still shows some symptoms that prevent us from declaring victory. We continue with checkups and with the hope that they will eventually find a way to help her fully recover. I trust that they will. My sincerest thanks to the medical team and all the staff who have cared for us during this very difficult time.
We went to the ophthalmologist and it was all very quick. Thank you.

All they care about is money. We took a little dog in who, while stretching, felt a sharp pain or something and suddenly lost mobility in both hind legs. We took him there, and after examining him and not doing any tests, they told us to do an MRI for almost two thousand euros, and if surgery was needed, it would be three thousand three hundred (we said we couldn't afford that). So they said, "Well, then let's weigh the dog because we'd have to put him to sleep" (while offering their condolences).... The dog is perfectly healthy. They charged us almost three hundred euros for the visit and did NOTHING. We asked if there wasn't another way, and they said, "Well, they could prescribe medication for him to take for 10 days, but that would be medicating him blindly." What a disgrace of a veterinary hospital. After taking him there, the dog regained mobility in one of his legs within a week. We took him to another vet where the cost was 80% cheaper. The dog had an x-ray, acupuncture, and laser treatment to try to solve his problem... It seems to me that this hospital or its employees are on commission, depending on how much money they make each month; they don't care at all about the animals' health.

Carlota, we have seen your review. Your name does not appear in our database, and since you did not describe your experience, we understand that it does not correspond to a situation that occurred in the hospital. You can write to us at comunicacion@hvpuchol.com.

I'm giving it one star because I can't give it a lower rating.
From the day I took my 5-month-old kitten to the emergency room until my last appointment with the specialists, it's been one disappointment after another.
The first time, as I mentioned, I took my cat to the emergency room because, although I didn't have a definitive diagnosis, I already had information that something wasn't right neurologically. My regular veterinary clinic told me that if I noticed any changes, I shouldn't hesitate to take her to the emergency room, specifically to this hospital because of how "professional" they are.

After explaining the situation to the receptionist and waiting in a waiting room from just after midnight until almost 3 a.m., with no one even bothering to give us any information or ask about my cat, I told them I was going to leave since they completely ignored me. At that very moment, they bothered to ask and alert an assistant to see me as soon as possible (so they wouldn't miss the opportunity to charge me, of course), but obviously I refused and chose to leave since I had an appointment at another clinic the next day (in just a few hours).
The receptionist herself told me, verbatim, that if you come to the emergency room and your pet isn't in a coma or convulsing, even if it's bleeding profusely or screaming in pain, you might still have to spend two hours in the waiting room with the animal in agony. In my case, obviously, since it's a neurological issue, it doesn't have these symptoms, implying that it wasn't a real emergency, but they still charge you for the emergency service.

After having to return to this hospital (much against my will) for neurological and ophthalmological evaluations of my cat, undergoing numerous tests (which I understand), still not receiving a diagnosis, and continuing with further tests—all of which I agreed to—last Monday, September 28th, I went back to confirm the results of two biopsies, crucial for starting treatment for my cat. They told me that one of them hadn't been sent, the more important of the two, in fact, because they BELIEVED the result of the first would be sufficient. They offered to send the other one if I wanted, since the result hadn't been what they expected. I had to pay who knows how much more, and above all, I wasted even more time that my pet DIDN'T have, because she was getting worse every week.

Obviously, I left feeling cheated and deceived, having had to endure a service and treatment far from humane and compassionate.

The conclusion of all this is that this clinic is primarily concerned with billing, billing, and billing, without considering the human aspect and the support so necessary in such an exhausting process as having a sick pet in the hands of "professionals" who are only concerned with prolonging the process and ordering more tests. I repeat, my complaint isn't so much about needing several of them, but about the precious time they made us waste.
Today, my cat is safe and sound because we took her to another hospital (Madrid Norte) as an emergency, since she reached her limit that same day. I will never tire of recommending this hospital to everyone, not because they don't have good professionals, but because of the appalling treatment and care.
Very professional, the best veterinarians

My experience with this hospital, although I ultimately decided not to go, was very negative.

I called seeking a specialist evaluation for my dog, who has a respiratory problem, and explained that before submitting him to any tests, I wanted a veterinarian to assess the case, review the tests he already had, and advise me on the possible causes and which tests might actually be indicated.

However, they told me I had to bring him in fasting because they planned to perform a CT scan and a bronchoscopy. All of this was before they had even seen the dog and before I had a veterinary evaluation with them.

Finally, I decided to get a second opinion and took my dog ​​to another clinic. After seeing him and simply listening to how he was breathing, the veterinarian told me that, based on the symptoms, there was approximately a 90% chance of laryngeal paralysis. He explained that to confirm this suspicion, the appropriate test would be a laryngoscopy, not to start directly with a CT scan and a bronchoscopy.

Precisely because it's a 12-year-old dog, I consider it especially important that before considering tests requiring sedation or anesthesia, the animal be clinically evaluated and the owner be informed about the suspected diagnosis, what they intend to rule out, and which test is truly necessary.

I can't evaluate the veterinary care during the consultation because I ultimately didn't attend, but I can evaluate the information and approach I received when requesting the appointment. And, in my case, they didn't inspire the necessary confidence to entrust my dog ​​to them.

Our veterinarian recommended a CT scan for our cat, Lía, at their hospital, even though we had been informed beforehand about the tests she had already undergone. They ignored our veterinarian's instructions and scheduled an initial consultation that included several unnecessary blood tests, as the purpose of the visit was to perform the CT scan.
During the subsequent visit for the CT scan, Isabel's attitude had changed; she was very distant and offered few explanations.
They told us we would have the results a week later. When the time came, we called several times to request the report, as they had only called to give us a brief explanation, and to this day we still haven't received it. Two weeks have passed since the CT scan. Thankfully, the veterinarian at our regular clinic provided us with the report (and explained it correctly) that Isabel had sent her, otherwise we would still be waiting.

I took my greyhound there for herniated disc surgery.

Overall, the care, surgery, and general well-being of the animal were excellent.

One thing I really dislike is the exorbitant price of the services. When you add up the consultation, surgery, tests, and daily stay, you're easily looking at 4,000 euros. And don't even think about going outside of regular hours—it's double the price (emergency). I'm not thinking about my own situation, but I can imagine how the average person wouldn't be able to afford a routine surgery for their pet. Pet insurance isn't a solution because in three years you'll end up paying the same amount as the surgery (or more).

In short, the service is very good, but the price is extremely high for surgery.

Regards

Edit: I'm adding some more information because I picked up my dog, Apolo, today from a very complicated tibia surgery. He'll need a second operation because a CT scan revealed it's more complex than expected, and all the staff at Puchol, especially the orthopedic surgeons, treated me wonderfully and explained everything my dog ​​needed.

Thank you so much!

---

I visited this hospital today with one of my dogs, Apolo, who needs leg surgery, and I was delighted with the treatment he received from all the staff and the specialist orthopedic surgeons. I'll be having my dog ​​operated on there, and it's wonderful to find professionals who explain the surgery my dog ​​needs in detail.

One night in the middle of the night, I had to rush my cat to the emergency vet. I took him to another emergency vet, and they referred me to Puchol Hospital. There were a lot of people waiting at reception, but in less than two minutes, my cat was being seen. The speed with which they handled everything was incredible. He was hospitalized for four days, and the communication was clear, even regarding scheduled appointments. Although it's not a place I'd want to take my own cats, I definitely recommend it.
Thank you so much for your top rating, Jimmy.
It's a comprehensive hospital with good professionals, but the waiting times are quite long, the costs are high, and if your dog is nervous or anxious, definitely don't go because it's always full.

This clinic, like almost 100% of veterinary clinics, is dedicated to making money by exploiting people's feelings. My experience was awful. They took 150 euros and were perfectly happy with that, without resolving anything that was wrong with my dog. They just told me to come back for more tests. I absolutely do not recommend this large clinic; all they want is MONEY 🫰🫰🫰🫰🫰🫰🫰🫰. I would be ashamed of them for deceiving people who love their dogs so much.

I want to express my heartfelt gratitude to Clínica Puchol, the entire ICU team, and especially to Dr. Isabel and Dr. Elena, veterinary internists, for everything you did for Chico, my fur baby.

We arrived when Chico was already very ill, after weeks without a clear diagnosis at another clinic. At Puchol, you acted quickly, identified what was wrong with him, and used every resource at your disposal to try and save him. Although my baby couldn't pull through, I know you did everything you could for him.

Thank you for your professionalism and also for the compassion with which you supported us during the most difficult days. I will always regret not having met you sooner.

To those of you seeking care for your pet: if something isn't right, go as soon as possible to a clinic with specialists and the resources to evaluate their case. Puchol will always be my go-to place. If another dog ever comes into my life, I will trust you.

Thank you for caring for Chico until the very end. ❤️
Dr. Vilagrasa, the ophthalmologist, is very good.

We were referred by our vet for a CT scan of one of our cats.
They wanted to do an initial consultation even though we had already told them we only wanted the CT scan.
At first they were friendly, but once we informed them through our vet that we only wanted the CT scan, their attitude deteriorated.
We are still waiting for the report, two weeks later.
When they realize they can't get any more money out of you, their treatment gets worse.

I want to sincerely thank the team at the veterinary hospital for the care our pet and we received. From the very first moment, they treated us with immense professionalism, warmth, and kindness, providing us with a great sense of calm during a time of worry.

It's clear they genuinely care about animals and are passionate about their work. They explained everything clearly, answered all our questions, and were attentive to my dog's progress at all times.
Thank you so much to the entire team for your care, dedication, and compassion. Without a doubt, this is a veterinary hospital I wholeheartedly recommend.
Thank you very much, Daniel.

We took our dog to this center because he was lethargic and weak. We were seen in the emergency room, and the veterinarian found he also had a fever and recommended his admission for monitoring and treatment. That's when our pet's ordeal began, with test after test, various treatments, and a progressive decline in his condition.

After nine days of hospitalization, some of them in the ICU, they confirmed he had endocarditis with a very serious prognosis.

I have no complaints about the veterinarians or the staff who cared for our pet; they were always attentive, kind, and empathetic. My only concern is whether they could have performed the echocardiogram before the eighth day, thus avoiding the animal's suffering and the cost of his stay.

The problem was with the hospital director. Specifically, during visiting hours on the seventh day, the receptionist told me I had some outstanding payments. I told her I would pay her the next day. At the end of the visit, I was told the director wanted to speak with me. Without further ado, he took me to his office and tersely told me that they didn't know what was wrong with our dog and that he wasn't aware of the medical details. He vehemently stated that "the rules must be followed, and we have to pay every day." I was stunned. I expected the call to discuss the animal's deteriorating condition and why they didn't know what was wrong with him after seven days in the hospital. I told him that I had already paid almost €3,000 that week and that the plan was to pay the remaining balance the next day, as we were expecting him to be discharged. He simply reiterated that "payment is daily," showing a complete lack of empathy and sensitivity to the anxiety, worry, and sadness we were experiencing.

Unfortunately, our dog's condition worsened on the last day, and they informed us of the diagnosis. They suggested we continue with further tests. Given the animal's condition—he was very lethargic and not eating—and because we didn't want to subject him to any more suffering, we requested a voluntary discharge. I paid the remaining balance and we took him home. Since then, back home and with the help of our veterinarian, he's surprisingly recovering well.

In short, our beloved pet left the hospital in very poor condition, much weaker and more depressed, and with a total bill exceeding €4,500.

I understand it's a business, but I'm left with the feeling that this hospital prioritizes financial matters over other very important aspects of a medical center. We won't be going back there.
Thank you very much, Cristina
Thank you so much
I had to take my cat to the emergency vet and the service was excellent. The waiting time was reasonable and Kokoro was treated exceptionally well.

A TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE.
We took our greyhound to the emergency clinic with an injured paw and in a lot of pain.
At reception, we were treated coldly, and they refused to treat him because he hadn't been referred by another veterinarian. When we insisted they see him, as the dog was suffering greatly, they ignored us and, with arrogance, zero empathy, and no regard for animals, told us it was the protocol and there was nothing they could do.
Without further ado, we went to another clinic where he received excellent care.
If you love your pet, don't waste your time bringing him here.
Thanks for everything

Get a bad reputation and then rest on your laurels. It used to be the best veterinary hospital in Madrid, but now it's in full decline. On the one hand, you have inexperienced trainees and very young people handling emergencies, where the most knowledge and professional skill are needed. The wait for appointments is incredibly long; the doctor is there, but often doesn't have a free office to see patients. The receptionists, with a few exceptions (the Latinas have been the friendliest), seem stressed and can even be rude. The specialist veterinarians (in my experience) are excellent and have access to technology that no one else has; they're leaders in many areas, but it's clear they've become very lax in their service, and I already know of more than two or three cases of negligence in triage. Please, go back to what you once were; we need a place to take our pets and be able to trust you in the most difficult moments.
Thank you so much
It's not cheap, but they are very professional and take excellent care of pets. They have all the specialties.

Excellent veterinary medical care.
Very attentive and empathetic.

I've been taking my dogs to Clínica Puchol since 2020, and the experience has been wonderful. I'm especially grateful to the specialists in ophthalmology: Miriam Caro; neurology: Alberto Muñiz; internal medicine: Isabel Rodríguez; surgery-traumatology: Pedro Godinho; and dermatology: Marina García for everything they've done for us and our wonderful canine family. Their kindness is outstanding, and their professionalism is top-notch. Despite being a multidisciplinary clinic, they haven't lost their personal touch or their friendly approach.
Thank you very much Thais
Professional team, excellent service. They advise you and take great care of you. It's a pleasure, I highly recommend them.
From the first visit to their operation, very fast, excellent
Delighted with the attention, treatment and how they arrived at the eye diagnosis for our water dog.

We want to express our enormous gratitude to **Puchol Veterinary Hospital** for the care, affection, and professionalism with which they treated our cat, **Nona**.

From the very first moment, we felt supported and in the best hands. We want to give special mention to **Carmen Gómez**, as well as the entire team in **Surgery and Traumatology, Ophthalmology, Rehabilitation, Hospitalization, Anesthesia, Dentistry, and Diagnostic Imaging**.

We were impressed by the professionalism and coordination of the entire team, but also by something equally important for those of us who love our animals as part of the family: the warmth, empathy, patience, and affection with which they treated both Nona and us.

In times of worry and uncertainty, finding professionals who explain things clearly, inspire confidence, and demonstrate a genuine commitment to the animal's well-being makes a huge difference.

**A heartfelt thank you to all the professionals at Puchol Veterinary Hospital for taking such wonderful care of Nona.** Our experience couldn't have been more positive, and we can only recommend your work and your team.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ **Absolutely recommended.**

We had "Koty", our Yorkshire Terrier, operated on and I only have words of "Gratitude" for all the staff, starting with Dr. Esther and her entire team! Caregivers, receptionists, even the cleaning staff

Thank you so much for helping my kitten through such a difficult time. She's doing very well thanks to your care and advice. A big thank you to the whole team, and especially to Carmen Gómez, the traumatologist, and Dr. José Luis Puchol. My kitten Nona is so happy now that she's recovered!
Thanks Jose

I was referred by my vet, with several consecutive appointments. At the last one, I arrived 10 minutes early. My cat wouldn't stop meowing because we travel so many kilometers, and they showed us to a room so she could be calm. At reception, they told us that they were seeing five patients with the same name that day, so I gave her last name to make it easier to find her. And it worked. We stayed in that room waiting. No one came. After waiting 30 minutes, plus the 10-minute grace period, I went out to ask what was happening. At reception, they told us they would call again. When we had been waiting a total of 43 minutes (plus 10), I decided that if no one came by 45 minutes, we would leave. And then a vet came. She told us she didn't know why, but they had marked her as seen. Without even seeing her. I still can't understand why they marked her as seen when our last name is uncommon, and especially why I highly doubt that patients with the same name would be seen at the same time and in the same specialty. Waiting 43 minutes (plus 10), and only because I went outside to see what was happening, seems morally unacceptable. But on top of that, they're a complete disaster with reports; I had to request one three times, and it took them 13 days to send it.
They have a terrible and serious organizational problem. And that's why I don't recommend them. I did really like their professionalism, though; they explain things, listen, and treat pets very well.

But the management and delivery of reports is awful. If I can avoid going back, I will. We travel so many kilometers only to be ignored.

Samson, blind for two years, was diagnosed with SARDS at Puchol Hospital by veterinarian Dr. Villagrasa and has been receiving checkups with him ever since. The care is superb and professional. Our dog and we feel safe and cared for. Thank you so much.
Later, we underwent a process involving coordinated efforts between the neurology and surgery teams. Following an MRI and CT scan, it was determined that our dog needed a very aggressive surgery to remove a benign tumor from his ear. Everything went wonderfully, and we will always be eternally grateful to Puchol Hospital, surgeon Pedro Godinho, neurologist Rafaela Drake, and their team members. A million thanks.

We were given an urgent appointment due to a problem with my dog, a 15-year-old, 2kg Yorkie. José Luis Puchol saw us immediately, performed the necessary tests, and provided a quick and professional solution. We had her operated on that same afternoon. The team of professionals is excellent; they work with a team of highly qualified specialists and use advanced technology. Their professionalism and experience are evident. The operation was a success, and everything was explained with complete clarity. I will definitely take her back. Many thanks to José Luis, the surgeon Juan Moreno, the anesthesiologist, Javier Justo, and the reception team for all their magnificent work.

We are delighted with the traumatology service in particular, and I must mention the wonderful Pedro, both professionally and personally: for his treatment of our Anuk, for his seriousness and clarity regarding the case, his magnificent work, and for explaining everything to us at every step without glossing over any possible outcomes. Without a doubt, this is the place with the best traumatologists in Madrid, and probably in all of Spain, I have no doubt.
Anuk had a problem with very crooked legs, and now his leg is straighter than a reed! xD Thank you from Anuk and his family.
Thank you very much, Francisco.

Whenever I've taken my dog ​​Gucci to the hospital, from getting him vaccinated to needing emergency surgery, we've always received fantastic care. I have complete confidence in this hospital and the professionals who work there.

We went to this emergency room because I was told they worked with our pet insurance, but when I spoke to my insurance company they said no. I contacted the hospital and they played dumb. They stole €600 from me. What a bunch of crooks!

I've been going to Puchol Veterinary Hospital for years. I first went with my previous pet for a dermatological problem with an infection complication due to negligence at another clinic. They not only resolved the problem quickly (it had been going on for months) but the vet also took care to follow up. Since then, unfortunately, I've had to see several specialists (traumatology, ophthalmology, emergency medicine, and general veterinary medicine), and I have nothing but praise for them. I've never felt overwhelmed with unnecessary diagnoses or tests, which is why now that I have a new Labrador puppy, I've been going back to them from the very beginning, making them our go-to vet. Thank you to the whole team!

We had to take our dog to the Puchol hospital after a car accident, and in both neurology and traumatology we received extraordinary care from José Luis Puchol and his colleagues. They treated us with great kindness, compassion, and professionalism. We will definitely recommend this veterinary hospital.

The best veterinary hospital for my dog's leg surgery!!! The staff is very friendly and always looking for the best, least invasive option to solve his problem!!!
I recommend it 1000% 😍
The treatment of our pet and us was wonderful. We brought her in critical condition and she's recovering phenomenally. Very professional.

We came to Puchol because we'd been told it was one of the best veterinary hospitals in Madrid, and the experience has certainly been excellent. We took our dachshund in because we noticed she was starting to walk strangely. They did an MRI and told us she needed surgery that same day for a herniated disc. We want to thank neurologist José Luis Caldera, who operated on Peeta, because his care and words were outstanding. She had to stay in the hospital for two nights, and on the day of our visit, we met María Martín, a hospitalization and nursing assistant, who gave us a very positive impression. We saw that she cared for our dog almost as if she were at home. Thank you so much, María! In short, we couldn't have chosen a better place to leave our dog. Thank you from the bottom of our hearts.

A very positive experience. The treatment of my dog ​​was exceptional, with attention to detail I'd never seen before, and the staff were very professional and attentive to every detail. My congratulations to all members of the team.

The hospital is very good in terms of facilities, and the veterinary and reception staff are very friendly. We went there for an emergency and were seen very quickly and very well. If I had to find fault with anything, it would be the price. I found it excessive. I know it's a business, but they should adjust their prices given the current economic situation with rising prices and inflation.
Veterinary hospital with excellent professionals and wonderful service. Excellent facilities. Punctual. Very good administrative and telephone service.

I don't doubt that it's an excellent hospital, but in my case, I think something went wrong. Tina, a two-kilo Chihuahua, was admitted on Sunday with seizures. We went to see her on Monday, and everything was fine; she hadn't had another seizure with the medication she'd been given. They even told us she'd be discharged on Tuesday with treatment if everything continued as it was. On Monday night at midnight, they called to tell us she had died. According to the specialist, everything was going perfectly, and the tragic outcome is inexplicable.
From my complete ignorance and humble opinion, I've come to the conclusion, based on details and spontaneous statements from emergency veterinarians and specialists, that the dog choked on the food they forced her to swallow with a syringe because she refused to eat. If a person in a hospital refuses to eat, you don't force-feed them with a syringe, for goodness sake! You feed them intravenously until they voluntarily tolerate the food.

Please excuse my reflection if it bothers anyone, but I'm so distressed that I feel I owe this comment to Tina.

My experience at this veterinary emergency clinic has been terrible, both because of the treatment I received and the lack of solutions.

I took my dog ​​there as an emergency because he had a perforation in his nasal septum, and blood was coming out of the wound when he breathed. Obviously, I was worried and expected, at the very least, attention, information, and a little empathy.

From the first moment, I was extremely surprised by the veterinarian's attitude: not even a "good evening." The treatment seemed cold, unpleasant, and lacking in empathy for someone working in an emergency service. They took my dog ​​away, and almost an hour passed before they came back up to explain what was happening.

They told me they would have to sedate him to shave the area and put in a stitch, but at the same time, they explained that they weren't sure how he would react to the sedation because of his age and because they didn't know for sure when he had eaten. Furthermore, they told me that even if they closed the wound that night, the surgeon would have to see him the next day, remove the stitch, and properly assess the depth of the injury.

Honestly, I didn't understand anything. They were proposing a procedure with a risk they themselves were pointing out, without being clear if it was the right solution, and knowing that the area would have to be operated on again the next day and reassessed.

In the end, I decided to leave with my dog. The worst part is that I left there without any solution, and as far as I could see, they hadn't even cleaned the wound. But I did save almost €200.

I perfectly understand that emergency veterinary care has a cost, and I'm willing to pay it when my dog ​​needs it. What I don't find acceptable is paying that amount and leaving with the same worry I came in with, without a solution, and with the feeling of having received unpleasant and very inhumane treatment.

I find it especially sad that in an emergency service, where people go scared and worried about their animals, something as basic as empathy, kindness, and a clear explanation of the options is lacking.

A very disappointing experience that I certainly wouldn't repeat.

My cat passed away at home, and I entrusted this hospital with her cremation, also ordering the printing of her paw prints. The hospital failed to carry out this latter order, and the handling of this irreparable error has been incredibly painful. They promised to contact me by phone to offer some explanation, but instead, I had to call them myself. Once again, they promised that the customer service representative would call the next day. However, she didn't, and the only thing I've received from this hospital employee is a cold and inhumane email during such a painful time as losing your companion after 20 years together. The mistake is irreparable, but the handling of the situation leaves much to be desired and speaks volumes about the human qualities of the people who work there. I trusted them, and they have failed in every way, demonstrating a lack of professionalism and an absence of empathy and sensitivity. Of course, the service was paid for in advance, and in none of their few communications have they even bothered to offer a refund, despite acknowledging that the error is theirs. All these actions and inactions tarnish the professionalism and quality of your center, since not only is clinical care important, but human care is essential, and in that respect, they leave much to be desired.

Unfortunately, my experience at this hospital has been completely negative. I've tried numerous times to post my review here, but they've either deleted it or prevented me from publishing it. Today I'm trying again, as it's been a year since the incident. I took my cat there on the recommendation of my veterinarian, and they tricked me into paying as much as possible, supposedly to find a different diagnosis for what was wrong with my cat than the one the veterinarian who referred me to. At Puchol Hospital, they told me it wasn't that diagnosis and didn't treat my cat for that problem (to this day, there's no doubt that the diagnosis from the veterinarian who referred me there was correct). They focused on confusing me to try to create a different diagnosis so they could charge me as much as possible. I was advised by other professionals in the field, and my family works in human healthcare. I have no doubt that the way this institution acted was completely against the life and well-being of animals, with the sole aim of making as much money as possible by exploiting someone else's misfortune.

People have to be paid for their work, but the work must be done properly, not by unscrupulously cheating to get paid more, endangering and harming the lives of animals.

I filed the corresponding complaint with the Madrid Veterinary Association (COLVEMA) with all the necessary documentation so that there is a record of what happened.
Clarification following Puchol Hospital's response to my review: COLVEMA expressly ruled in writing that this was a matter of civil liability, and if the parties could not reach an agreement, the matter should go to court.
